items.title: 61124_Mario Bauza oral history interview
items.q: Heavy Man, he wrote -- he (inaudible) he knew already.

ctx.x: Well, you know, what I'm getting at is then it became -- then people started writing suites. Chico wrote suites. Gil Fuller (phonetic), I think, also. And you have the time when you were from about "Afro-Jazz Suite", then you had Afro-Cuban suites and --

See, that's when -- we lose the boat. I had this here problem with Heavy Man (phonetic). Heavy Man, he wrote -- he (inaudible) he knew already. So he wrote some things for his recording. It brought -- he brought -- he had

the same problem. You don't say Afro-Cuban just to use the name (inaudible). You like to know (inaudible). And if you didn't know (inaudible) you lost. And they feel that really you just -- is on the bongos. The rhythm go and the part and the (inaudible) bass player. You've got to be able to know how to (inaudible) how to write your name in that particular number, in that particular (inaudible), and none of them ever learned that.
